sector: Retail and commercial banking, from POS agent to national bank
howTheBusinessMakesMoney: A bank borrows cheaply from depositors and lends or invests at higher rates. The gap, net interest margin, is most of its income; fees on transfers, cards and cash add the rest. The regulator locks part of every deposit as a reserve, demands a capital cushion against bad loans, and insures small savers. A POS agent earns only fees for moving cash on behalf of a licensed bank and may not keep deposits. Profit = spread + fees - staff, branches and bad loans.

caseStudies.scale: Largest US bank: $185bn revenue, $57bn net income and $4.4tn assets in 2025; CET1 capital ratio 14.5%.
caseStudies.lesson: Scale wins on cost of funds: a huge base of cheap everyday deposits funds loans, and a capital ratio well above the minimum lets it keep lending when others freeze. Reward a thick capital cushion.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: $112bn revenue, of which $62bn net interest income; net income $30.5bn.
caseStudies.lesson: About 45% of revenue is fees (cards, payments, advice), so income holds up when rates fall. The game should let fee products grow into a second engine beside the spread.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: N1.26tn profit before tax, N24tn deposits, N11tn gross loans, NPL ratio 3.8%, capital adequacy 25%.
caseStudies.lesson: Lends under half its deposits and keeps liquidity at 71%: with 45% locked at the central bank and T-bills paying well, a Nigerian bank wins by being careful, not by lending everything.

caseStudies.scale: 2025: over 14bn transactions worth about N412tn, 6m+ active businesses, over N1tn lent to small firms.
caseStudies.lesson: Started as POS and agent rails, earned tiny fees on huge volume, then used that data to lend and hold deposits under a microfinance licence. Copy the kiosk-to-licence ladder.

regulation.unitedStates: Charter from the OCC (national) or a state, with Federal Reserve oversight and FDIC insurance approval; capital is set case by case, not one fixed figure.
regulation.nigeria: CBN: N500bn international, N200bn national, N50bn regional (recapitalisation ended 31 Mar 2026). MFBs: N50m unit up to N5bn national.

regulation.unitedStates: Federal Reserve reserve requirement is 0% for all depository institutions since 26 March 2020.
regulation.nigeria: CBN CRR: 45% of deposits for commercial banks, 16% merchant banks, 75% non-TSA public deposits; kept in Sept 2026 as MPR cut to 23%.

regulation.unitedStates: FDIC insures up to $250,000 per depositor per bank per ownership category and resolves failed banks.
regulation.nigeria: NDIC (2024): N5m per depositor at commercial banks, N2m at microfinance, mortgage and payment service banks; covers about 99% of depositors.

regulation.unitedStates: Fed, OCC and FDIC apply Basel III: CET1 minimum 4.5% plus buffers; 'well capitalised' needs total capital of 10% or more.
regulation.nigeria: CBN capital adequacy minimum 10% for national banks, 15% for international (from prior knowledge, not re-verified this round).

regulation.unitedStates: No agent banking regime; non-bank cash and transfer networks need state money transmitter licences and FinCEN registration.
regulation.nigeria: CBN: N1.2m per agent per day, N100,000 cash-out per customer per day, geo-fenced devices; exclusivity and location rules from 1 Apr 2026.

regulation.unitedStates: Federal Reserve sets the fed funds target; Treasury sells T-bills that banks hold as zero-risk liquid assets.
regulation.nigeria: CBN MPR 23% (Sept 2026); DMO/CBN sell T-bills, 364-day stop rate 15.85% in Oct 2026; banks hold them for liquidity.

gameRules.name: Deposit Waterfall
gameRules.rule: Each N100 deposited: reserve R locked at 0% (R=0 at kiosk, 10 at MFB, 45 at bank stages), till T>=5 kept in vault, rest free. Player splits free funds between loans L and T-bills B with slider; L+B=100-R-T.
gameRules.playerFeels: Almost half my money is locked away; every naira left must work hard.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: CBN 45% CRR for commercial banks plus liquidity buffer; MFB reserve is a game value.

gameRules.name: The Spread
gameRules.rule: Monthly: income = L x 2.5% (bank) or 3% (MFB) + B x 1.33% + fees; interest cost = savings deposits x 0.67%; current accounts (60% of deposits) cost 0%. Net = income - interest - salaries - provisions.
gameRules.playerFeels: Cheap current accounts are gold; expensive savers squeeze my margin.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Lending near 30% a year, 364-day T-bill 15.85%, savings near 8%, NIM 7-10%.

gameRules.name: Loans Must Come Home
gameRules.rule: Loan term 6 months. Repay chance shown on loan card: 80% unchecked, 97% with Credit Officer check. Default: principal lost, 30% recovered politely after 3 months. NPL% = defaulted / total loans.
gameRules.playerFeels: Fast loans are tempting but the credit check pays for itself.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NPL ratios 3.8%-5% at large Nigerian banks; recovery rates estimated.

gameRules.name: Examiner Limits
gameRules.rule: If NPL > 5%: no new loans until <= 5%. Capital ratio = equity / (loans x 100% + B x 0%). Below 10% (15% international): no new loans or branches; below 5% for 30 days: licence suspended.
gameRules.playerFeels: I must keep a cushion of my own money, not just customers' money.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Basel risk weights, CBN 10%/15% CAR, 5% NPL prudential line.

gameRules.name: Trust and the Run
gameRules.rule: Trust 0-100, starts 70. Daily withdrawals = deposits x 1%; if trust < 50 add (50 - trust) x 0.2% of deposits. Unpaid customer: trust -10. Fully paid day during run: +5. Run ends at trust 60.
gameRules.playerFeels: One empty till starts a queue; paying every customer calmly ends it.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: Deposit runs driven by confidence; liquidity buffers stop them.

gameRules.name: Liquidity Ladder
gameRules.rule: Withdrawals paid in order: till, then sell T-bills same day at 1% loss, then central bank loan at 23.5% a year against T-bills, then sell loans to another bank at 30% loss (3 days). Reserve stays locked.
gameRules.playerFeels: T-bills are my fire extinguisher; loans cannot be turned into cash quickly.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: CBN standing lending facility at MPR + 0.5% (+50/-300 corridor); illiquid loan books.

gameRules.name: Insured Sticker
gameRules.rule: From MFB stage the insurance sticker shows: savers with game balance <= N2m (MFB) or <= N5m (bank) run at half speed. Premium = 0.35% of deposits a year, paid monthly.
gameRules.playerFeels: Insurance costs a little but keeps small savers calm.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: NDIC cover N2m MFB, N5m DMB; premium rate is an estimate.

gameRules.name: Agent Float and Fees
gameRules.rule: Kiosk: cash-out fee N100 per N5,000 (2%); network keeps 0.5% capped at N100 per transaction. Float pre-funded; kiosk closes when moved total hits N1.2m/day or any customer hits N100,000/day.
gameRules.playerFeels: Busy days are capped; I plan float runs, not just sales.
gameRules.simplifiedFrom: CBN agent caps; street agent fees; network charge estimated.

uniqueMechanics.name: Balance Sheet Board
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Each month drags sliders to split free funds between loans, T-bills and till cash, watching margin, liquidity and capital ratio change live before confirming.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Stacked bar of deposits (reserve, till, T-bills, loans) with three gauges: margin, liquidity, capital ratio.

uniqueMechanics.name: Loan Desk
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: Reviews borrower cards showing amount, rate and open repay chance; sends the Credit Officer to check or approves fast; follows late loans with polite reminders.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Card queue with repay odds bar, approve/check/decline buttons, and loan book list with NPL% meter.

uniqueMechanics.name: Run on the Bank
uniqueMechanics.whatThePlayerDoes: When trust falls, a queue forms at the door; player pays from till, sells T-bills or borrows from the central bank to pay everyone until trust recovers.
uniqueMechanics.screenNeeded: Banking hall with live queue, trust meter, till counter and liquidity ladder buttons with their cost shown.

failureStates.what: Float runs out at the kiosk
failureStates.trigger: Cash on hand falls below N10,000 before 2pm
failureStates.consequence: Cash-out closed; queue walks away, daily revenue drops about 50%
failureStates.recovery: Run to the float box (costs 1 hour) or hire a runner; raise morning float

failureStates.trigger: NPL ratio above 5% of total loans
failureStates.consequence: No new loans; examiner visit; interest income shrinks as loans repay
failureStates.recovery: Recover or write off defaults; approve only checked loans until NPL is 5% or less

failureStates.trigger: Capital ratio below 10% (15% at international stage)
failureStates.consequence: No new loans, branches or stage upgrade
failureStates.recovery: Retain profit (no dividend), raise equity, shift funds from loans to T-bills

failureStates.trigger: Trust below 50, or any day with an unpaid withdrawal
failureStates.consequence: Withdrawals rise up to 11% of deposits a day; forced T-bill and loan sales lose money
failureStates.recovery: Pay everyone via liquidity ladder; 2 fully paid days lift trust by 10; run ends at trust 60

failureStates.trigger: Capital ratio below 5% for 30 days or a run that cannot be paid
failureStates.consequence: Insurer pays small savers; bank closes; player drops back one stage
failureStates.recovery: Rebuild from prior stage with kept agent network and 25% of remaining equity

balanceNotes: Payback: kiosk 3 months, agent shop 6, unit MFB 46, state MFB 52, regional 42, national 32, international 23, people's bank 1. The MFB-to-regional jump (N1.2bn to N55bn) is where players stall; give investor rounds or allow capital from retained profit plus listing. The 45% reserve halves the bank-stage margin, so tune the loan rate and current-account share first, then default rates. Keep runs rare (1 in 12 months) unless the player neglects till cash.
openQuestions: Should the 45% reserve hit hard at regional stage, or phase in from 20% so the jump from microfinance feels fair?
Can players raise outside equity (investor rounds, listing) or only use retained profit to meet each capital pad?
Should the policy rate move with real CBN decisions via events, or stay fixed at 23% for predictable balance?
Does licence suspension drop the player one stage, or end the business and keep only cash?
